entries.title: Software Requirements Specification
entries.summary: Formal Software Requirements Specification for M2 covering system background, user use cases, and key example flows.
entries.body:
![SRS Use Case Diagram](images/docs/srs-use-case-diagram.png)

# Software Requirements Specification (M2)

Revision History:

| Date | Author | Description |
| ---- | ------ | ----------- |
| Apr 1 | Lee | Add use cases |

## 0. Background

Our team is responsible for designing and developing a **web-based platform** with the primary functions of **receiving sensor data**, **conducting motion analysis**, and **providing health recommendations**. The system users primarily include **registered users** (who upload motion data), **doctors** (who provide the recommendations) and **administrators** (who monitor and manage the data).
## 1. Use Cases

### 1.1. Patient

| Case | Description | Trigger condition |
| ---- | ----------- | ----------------- |
| **Register** | Users can register as platform members by providing basic information. | The user clicks the "Register" button, and the system starts the registration process. |
| **Log in** | The user inputs their account and password for authentication, and after successful authentication, they enter the platform. | The user clicks the "Login" button, and the system starts the login process. |
| **View Rehabilitation Plan** | Patients can view their personalized rehabilitation plan, including scheduled exercises, frequency, and duration. | The user clicks "My Plan" on the dashboard. |
| **Execute Motion with Guidance** | Patients can view motion demonstration videos or animations and receive step-by-step guidance during exercise execution. | The user selects a specific exercise and clicks "Start Exercise". |
| **View Rehabilitation Records** | Patients can view historical rehabilitation records, including exercise completion status, motion quality scores, and progress trends. | The user clicks "History" or "My Records". |
| **Receive Real-time Feedback** | Patients receive immediate feedback on motion execution quality during or after exercise, including correction suggestions. | The system detects motion completion or deviation during exercise. |
| **Set Rehabilitation Goals** | Patients can set personal rehabilitation goals (e.g., weekly exercise frequency, motion accuracy targets) and track achievement progress. | The user clicks "Set Goals" in the goal tracking section. |
| **View Achievements & Motivations** | Patients can view earned achievement badges, streaks, and receive motivational messages based on their progress. | The user clicks "Achievements" or receives system-triggered motivational notifications. |
| **Receive Messages & Notifications** | Patients can receive system messages, doctor notifications, appointment reminders, and progress alerts. | The system pushes a notification when new messages arrive or important events occur. |

### 1.2. Doctor

| Case | Description | Trigger condition |
| ---- | ----------- | ----------------- |
| **Register** | Doctors can register as platform members by providing professional credentials and basic information. | The doctor clicks the "Register as Doctor" button, and the system starts the registration process. |
| **Log in** | The doctor inputs their account and password for authentication, and after successful authentication, they enter the platform. | The doctor clicks the "Login as Doctor" button, and the system starts the login process. |
| **View Patient Management Panel** | Doctors can view the list and basic information of all assigned patients. | The doctor clicks "Patient Management" after logging in. |
| **View Data Visualization & Analysis** | Doctors can view patients' motion data charts, trends, and statistical analysis. | The doctor enters a patient's detail page and clicks "Data Analysis". |
| **Playback Motion Capture** | Doctors can replay motion capture videos or data trajectories uploaded by patients. | The doctor enters a patient's motion record and clicks "Playback". |
| **Generate Smart Report** | The system automatically generates motion analysis reports; doctors can review and modify them. | The doctor clicks the "Generate Report" button. |
| **Handle Anomaly Detection Alerts** | Doctors receive abnormal motion alerts, review details, and provide recommendations. | The system detects abnormal motion and pushes a notification. |
| **Adjust Treatment Plan** | Doctors can modify or create new rehabilitation plans based on patient data. | The doctor enters a patient's detail page and clicks "Edit Treatment Plan". |
| **Collaboration & Discussion** | Doctors can discuss patient cases with other medical team members. | The doctor clicks the "Collaboration" entry. |

### 1.3. Administration

| Case | Description | Trigger condition |
| ---- | ----------- | ----------------- |
| **Register** | Administrators can register as platform members (typically created by super admin or system initialization). | The super admin clicks "Create Administrator", and the system starts the registration process. |
| **Log in** | The administrator inputs their account and password for authentication, and after successful authentication, they enter the management platform. | The administrator clicks the "Login as Administrator" button, and the system starts the login process. |
| **Manage Data Interfaces** | Administrators can view and manage API interface status and call logs. | The administrator enters the "Interface Management" page. |
| **Manage Sensor Devices** | Administrators can monitor sensor device status and handle device binding exceptions. | The administrator enters the "Sensor Management" page. |
| **Manage AI Models** | Administrators can manage AI analysis model versions, updates, and deployments. | The administrator enters the "AI Model Management" page. |
| **View Logs & Monitoring** | Administrators can view system operation logs, performance monitoring, and anomaly alerts. | The administrator enters the "Log Monitoring" page. |
| **Manage Permissions & Roles** | Administrators can manage user roles, access permissions, and data permissions. | The administrator enters the "Permission Management" page. |
| **Data Export & Backup** | Administrators can perform system data backup and export data on demand. | The administrator enters the "Data Management" page and clicks "Backup/Export". |
## 2. Key Examples

### 2.1. User Register

#### 2.1.1. Basic info

- **Reference to Use Case** 1.1.
- **Version:** 0.1
- **Created:** Apr 1
- **Authors:** Lee
- **Source:** Web Interface
- **Actors:** Patient
- **Goal:** Allow users to become platform members through registration.
- **Summary:** New users input basic information, and the system validates and creates a user account.
- **Trigger:** User clicks the "Register" button.
- **Frequency:** Depends on the number of new users.
- **Precondition:** The system permits new user registration.
- **Postconditions:** The system returns registration success information and creates an account.

#### 2.1.2. Basic Flow

| Actor | System |
| ----- | ------ |
| User fills in registration information (username, password, email, age, etc.) | |
| User clicks the "Register" button | |
| | **Validate** that the username is unique |
| | **Validate** that the password meets format requirements |
| | **Create user account** and store in the database |
| | **Return success information** to the interface |
| User receives registration success notification | |

#### 2.1.3. Alternative Flow

| Actor | System |
| ----- | ------ |
| | **Username already exists**, return "Username already taken" |
| | **Password does not meet format requirements**, return "Password must contain at least 8 characters, including letters and numbers" |
| | **Email format is invalid**, return "Invalid email format" |
| | **Required fields are missing**, return "Please fill in all required fields" |

### 2.2. Sensor Connection

#### 2.2.1. Basic Info

- **Reference to Use Case** 1.1. (Patient - Execute Motion with Guidance)
- **Version:** 1.0
- **Created:** Apr 1
- **Authors:** Lee
- **Source:** Sensor Device / Mobile SDK
- **Actors:** Logged-in Patient
- **Goal:** Allow patients to connect sensor devices to the platform and upload motion data.
- **Summary:** Users connect sensor devices via Bluetooth/WiFi; the system validates the connection and begins receiving motion data streams.
- **Trigger:** User clicks the "Connect Device" button.
- **Frequency:** Before each rehabilitation training session.
- **Precondition:** User is logged in; sensor device is powered on and has sufficient battery; device is within connection range.
- **Postconditions:** The system successfully binds the sensor to the user account and begins receiving and storing motion data.

#### 2.2.2. Basic Flow

| Actor | System |
| ----- | ------ |
| User clicks the "Connect Sensor" button | |
| User selects device type (e.g., IMU sensor, smartwatch) | |
| | **Scan** for nearby available sensor devices |
| | **Return list** of available devices |
| User selects the target device from the list | |
| | **Initiate pairing request** and verify device identity |
| | **Confirm successful pairing** |
| | **Display** "Device Connected" status |
| | **Begin receiving sensor data stream** |
| User starts training session | |

#### 2.2.3. Alternative Flow

| Actor | System |
| ----- | ------ |
| | **No devices found**, display "No devices found. Please check Bluetooth/WiFi." |
| | **Device pairing fails**, display "Pairing failed. Please ensure the device is discoverable." |
| | **Connection interrupted**, display "Connection lost. Attempting to reconnect..." |
| | **Low sensor battery**, display "Low battery. Please charge the device." |

entries.title: First Version of the M2 Portal Is Now Online
entries.summary: On March 31, the first version of the M2 portal officially went live, giving the team a more stable public-facing space for presentation and process tracking.
entries.body:
On March 31, the first version of the M2 portal officially went live. With this launch, the team gained a more stable public-facing space for presentation and process tracking.

## A New Team Hub

Unlike a single page or one-off deliverable, the portal works as an ongoing team hub. It gives M2 a place not only to show pages, but also to gather records, links, intermediate outputs, and the growing documentation of the work itself.

## Why It Matters

As a project develops, what matters is not only what has been built, but also whether the process can be made understandable to others. The portal marks a shift: M2 is not only building interfaces, but also building a clearer narrative and structure around its own work.

## Links

Live Page:
https://dsd2026-team-m2.github.io/project-portal/

Repository:
https://github.com/DSD2026-Team-M2/project-portal

---

Posted by Team M2 · DSD 2025-2026 · UTAD × JLU

entries.title: M2 Portal 首版上线
entries.summary: 3 月 31 日，M2 的第一版 portal 正式上线，团队也由此拥有了一个更稳定的公开展示与过程记录空间。
entries.body:
3 月 31 日，M2 的第一版 portal 正式上线。随着这一入口建立，团队开始拥有一个更加稳定的公开展示与过程记录空间。

## A New Team Hub

相比单个页面或单次展示，portal 更像是团队持续建设中的“总入口”。它不仅承载页面本身，也承载记录、链接、阶段性成果以及后续逐步补充的过程材料。

## Why It Matters

项目推进到一定阶段后，真正重要的不只是做出了什么，还包括能否把过程整理清楚、让外部成员快速理解团队做了什么、为什么这样做、下一步要去哪里。portal 的上线，意味着 M2 在“开发”之外，也开始建设自己的叙事和组织能力。

## Links

Live Page:
https://dsd2026-team-m2.github.io/project-portal/

Repository:
https://github.com/DSD2026-Team-M2/project-portal

---

Posted by Team M2 · DSD 2025-2026 · UTAD × JLU

entries.title: Portal System Design Outline
entries.summary: Design outline for routed pages, generated content indexes, language fallback, markdown rendering and static holiday data.

actionItems.task: Confirm content index field coverage before the final build review.

entries.body:
## Architecture

The portal uses a routed React shell with lightweight reusable sections and content-rendering pages.

## Content Pipeline

- Scan markdown files under `content/<locale>/...`
- Parse front matter into a unified index
- Validate required fields and duplicate slugs
- Render lists and detail pages from generated JSON

## Rendering Rules

- UI strings come from i18n JSON.
- Content lookup falls back to English when the selected locale is missing.
- Markdown headings receive stable anchors for direct linking.

entries.title: First Mockup of the Main Project Interface Goes Live
entries.summary: Also on March 24, the first mockup of M2's main project interface went online, turning discussion-stage ideas into a visible and reviewable prototype.
entries.body:
Also on March 24, the first mockup of M2's main project interface went online. It was still an early version, but it already transformed ideas under discussion into something visible and reviewable.

## A First Visible Prototype

The value of this mockup is simple: it gave the team a concrete interface to look at, discuss, and iterate on. In web development, many design and usability questions only become clear once a page actually exists.

## Why This Matters

With a first working mockup in place, team discussions no longer had to rely only on abstract descriptions. Layout, interaction, data display, and user perspective could now be discussed against a visible prototype, which made communication much more efficient.

## Links

Repository:
https://github.com/DSD2026-Team-M2/project-main-web

Live Page:
https://dsd2026-team-m2.github.io/project-main-web/#/p/p-001/trends

---

entries.title: Team M2 Formed - Initial Roles Now Assigned
entries.summary: On March 24, Team M2 was fully formed and its initial role distribution was confirmed, turning an informal grouping into a working structure for coordinated delivery.
entries.body:
On March 24, Team M2 was fully formed and the initial role distribution was confirmed. The team moved from an early informal grouping into a structure that could actually support coordinated work.

## The Team

Five members have now been confirmed for Team M2:

- Lee (Lee-YihangLI-55230714)
- Kika (Vasconcelos Francisca)
- Shu (Hai-DuhaiXU-21230517)
- BFD_QT (Congming-CongmingLI-38230227)
- Hai (Shu-ShuWANG-35232116)

## Initial Role Assignment

The initial working structure of M2 is as follows:

- Lee - Project Manager  
  Responsible for task allocation, overall progress, cadence control, requirement alignment, and external communication.

- Hai - System Architect and Designer  
  Responsible for page design, requirement analysis, and user research.

- BFD_QT - Web Maintainer  
  Responsible for developing and maintaining the team website, and for documenting the development process and progress of the project.

- Kika - Vice PM / Programmer  
  Works asynchronously from Portugal, coordinates with the PM, and implements user interface logic for static rehabilitation data and historical records.

- Shu - Programmer  
  Responsible for implementing and displaying 3D reconstruction based on sensor-collected data.

## From Group to Working Team

With both members and roles now in place, M2 stopped being only a list of names and became a team able to collaborate around the Clinical Web Dashboard direction in a more concrete and deliverable way.

---

Posted by Team M2 · DSD 2025-2026 · UTAD × JLU

entries.title: Team Structure Proposal Shared by M1 Lead Pinhel
entries.summary: During March, Pinhel from Team M1 shared the Team Structure DSD proposal, outlining a six-team division for the wider DSD project and giving M2 an earlier view of system-wide collaboration boundaries.
entries.body:
During March, Pinhel, the leader of Team M1 on the Portuguese side, shared a document titled `Team Structure DSD.pdf` and proposed a six-team division for the wider DSD project.

## A Cross-Team Proposal

At the start of the course, most teams only had a broad understanding of what the project was about. This document pushed the discussion further by addressing a more practical question: who would do what, how teams would connect, and how parallel development could become possible.

## Why It Mattered to M2

For M2, the proposal did more than introduce an organisational idea. It helped us understand our likely place in the overall system much earlier, and gave us a clearer sense of the collaboration boundaries and dependencies that would shape our later work.

## Reference

[1] Pinhel. *Team Structure DSD* [PDF]. March 2026. Available in the repository attachment: [Team Structure DSD.pdf](files/team-structure-dsd.pdf).

---

Posted by Team M2 · DSD 2025-2026 · UTAD × JLU

entries.body:
3 月期间，葡萄牙方 M1 队队长 Pinhel 分享了 `Team Structure DSD.pdf`，提出了面向整个 DSD 项目的六组分工建议，为后续各队定位和协作方式提供了更清晰的参照。

## A Cross-Team Proposal

在课程刚启动的阶段，大家对整体项目还停留在“知道要做什么”的层面，而这份文档则进一步回答了“谁来做、怎么接、如何并行”这些更实际的问题。它让整个项目从概念描述，开始走向结构化组织。

## Why It Mattered to M2

对于 M2 来说，这份提案的意义不只是“看见一个方案”，更重要的是帮助我们更早理解自己在全项目中的位置，以及未来与其他队伍之间可能形成的接口关系和协作边界。

## Reference

[1] Pinhel. *Team Structure DSD* [PDF]. March 2026. 仓库附件见：[Team Structure DSD.pdf](files/team-structure-dsd.pdf)。

---

entries.title: Requirement Analysis
entries.summary: Baseline requirement analysis defining the portal as a reporting, documentation and collaboration hub rather than a product site.
entries.body:
## Scope

Define the role, boundaries and minimum page structure of the project portal.

## Must Answer

- What is the overall project?
- What is the portal for?
- What is M2 responsible for?
- Where are logs, milestones, documents and deliverables located?

## Constraints

- The portal must not impersonate the main product web application.
- The implementation should stay simple enough for a Vite, React and TypeScript learner to maintain.
- Content updates should rely on markdown and generated indexes wherever possible.

entries.title: Análise de Requisitos
entries.summary: Análise base que define o portal como centro de relatório, documentação e colaboração, e não como site do produto.
entries.body:
## Âmbito

Definir o papel, as fronteiras e a estrutura mínima de páginas do `project-portal`.

## Perguntas obrigatórias

- O que é o projeto no seu todo?
- Para que serve o portal?
- O que está sob responsabilidade da M2?
- Onde estão os registos, marcos, documentos e entregáveis?

entries.title: 需求分析
entries.summary: 定义 portal 的角色、边界与最小页面结构，明确它是汇报、文档与协作中枢，而不是产品站。
entries.body:
## 范围

定义 project-portal 的定位、边界、信息架构与最低实现范围。

## 必须回答的问题

- 这是什么项目？
- portal 是做什么的？
- M2 负责什么？
- 日志、里程碑、文档和交付物在哪里？

## 约束

- portal 不能冒充主产品网页。
- 实现必须足够简单，适合正在学习 Vite、React、TypeScript 的同学继续维护。
- 内容更新应优先通过 markdown 和生成脚本完成。

entries.title: Course Begins - First Cross-Site Video Meeting Held
entries.summary: The DSD course officially started on March 19, and members from China and Portugal held their first cross-site video meeting to align on the project, collaboration model, and initial rhythm.
entries.body:
The DSD course officially began on March 19. Members from China and Portugal joined the first video meeting to get a shared understanding of the Limb Motion Recognition and Assistant project, its collaboration model, and the initial working rhythm.

## Kickoff Meeting

This meeting was mainly about alignment rather than implementation. It gave the team a first common picture of the project goals and also made the realities of distributed work immediately visible: time zones, communication cadence, and role coordination would all shape the work ahead.

## First Leadership Decision

At this stage, detailed group responsibilities had not yet been assigned. The only role confirmed during the kickoff was the group leader, and Lee was selected to take that position and coordinate the team's early organisation and communication.

## What Comes Next

The course had officially started, but the working structure was still taking shape. The next step for M2 was to complete team formation under a clearer overall framework and begin moving from orientation into concrete work.

---

entries.title: 课程启动 - 首次跨国视频会议举行
entries.summary: DSD 课程于 3 月 19 日正式开始，中国与葡萄牙成员完成了第一次跨国视频会议，对项目背景、协作方式和初步节奏进行了统一认识。
entries.body:
DSD 课程于 3 月 19 日正式开始。中国与葡萄牙两地成员进行了第一次视频会议，共同了解 Limb Motion Recognition and Assistant 项目的整体背景、合作方式与初步节奏。

## Kickoff Meeting

这次会议更像一次真正意义上的开场。大家先对项目的总体目标进行了统一认识，也对跨国协作的基本现实有了第一轮直观感受：时差、沟通节奏、角色协同，都会在之后的开发中持续影响团队的工作方式。

## First Leadership Decision

在这一阶段，各组的细化分工尚未正式落定。会议上唯一率先确认的是组长人选，最终由 Lee 担任组长，负责团队的前期组织、沟通协调与后续对接。

## What Comes Next

课程已经启动，但真正的团队结构还在形成之中。接下来的任务，是在更明确的整体框架下完成队伍组建，并逐步把讨论从“了解项目”推进到“开始动手”。

---
